cards.title: Sugar myths, served with mithai
cards.body: Every family has a diabetes expert. Here are five common myths, and why the real answers come from the doctor.

cards.title: Myth: sugar is fine, so stop
cards.body: Good readings often mean the treatment is working. Stopping or cutting doses on your own can undo that. Talk to the doctor first.

cards.title: Myth: insulin means you failed
cards.body: Insulin is a treatment, not a punishment. Doctors suggest it based on what the body needs. Ask them to explain why.

cards.title: Myth: sweets now, extra tablet later
cards.body: Medicines aren't a pass for mithai. Never adjust a dose to cover food unless the doctor has given you a plan for that.

cards.title: Myth: the tablets damage kidneys
cards.body: Uncontrolled sugar itself can harm the kidneys. If you're worried about a medicine, ask the doctor about it and about regular tests. Don't stop it alone.

cards.title: Myth: no symptoms, no problem
cards.body: High sugar can be silent, so regular tests matter. Low sugar can show as shaking, sweating or confusion. Know the doctor's plan, and get urgent help if it doesn't settle.

cards.title: Keep the doctor in the loop
cards.body: Bring readings, medicines and questions to every visit. The best answer to a myth is a two-minute question to the person who prescribed it.

takeaway: Don't change diabetes medicines based on readings, sweets or rumours. Track sugar and ask the doctor.
share: Send this to the family group before the next mithai debate.
